decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom represents heavy development investment and a publicly announced international rollout, so management stays committed and attributes slow uptake to the long procurement cycles of proton centers.
Small volume chambers are core precision-dosimetry instruments with low maintenance cost that fit the firm's measurement identity, so there is no reason to withdraw it.
Despite overlapping with Product B, the sunk certification and calibration investment and the need to justify the launch lead management to keep it in the portfolio.
The multi-model standard clinical chamber line is central to the established calibration and dosimetry business and is retained.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and connected QA workflows, making it strategically aligned with the announced platform direction.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments with steady demand backed by accredited calibration services, so the firm keeps it.
